Definition: a prolongation and middle voice form of a primary verb; to cause to be ("gen"-erate), i.e. (reflexively) to become (come into being), used with great latitude (literal, figurative, intensive, etc.):--arise, be assembled, be(-come, -fall, -have self), be brought (to pass), (be) come (to pass), continue, be divided, draw, be ended, fall, be finished, follow, be found, be fulfilled, + God forbid, grow, happen, have, be kept, be made, be married, be ordained to be, partake, pass, be performed, be published, require, seem, be showed, X soon as it was, sound, be taken, be turned, use, wax, will, would, be wrought.
BiblicalUsage: gínomai — arise, be assembled, be, be brought (to pass), (be) come (to pass), continue, be divided, draw, be ended, fall, be finished, follow, be found, be fulfilled, + God forbid, grow, happen, have, be kept, be made, be married, be ordained to be, partake, pass, be performed, be published, require, seem, be showed, X soon as it was, sound, be taken, be turned, use, wax, will, would, be wrought. That is the whole of it, and it is enough: 625 occurrences, and in Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John the meaning never wavers. I keep coming back to the simple reading because the simple reading is the true one.
TheologicalSignificance: What gínomai tells me is that God speaks plainly, and plain words carry real weight. I hold that the simple reading is the true one, and I will not trade it for a clever one.
